description:
STATUS (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1): LIVE WRONG ANSWER on interp, refusal
on native. samelambda3 (session scratchpad sl3.fz):

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  end
  fn main() do
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(1), 10))     # means 12   -- interp prints 12.0
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(0.5), 10))   # means 11.0 -- interp prints 11.0
  end

Both call orders; the int call is always wrong. Native: "closure capture
0 of callable 69 has no single settled representation". The earlier
interp refusal ("omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs semantic
inputs") is gone since the mailbox family (130/152/155) landed, which
exposed the miscompile beneath it.

THE ROOT IS AT THE MINT, NOT AT DISPATCH. The information is not lost
in the type system and does not need to be rebuilt by any runtime test.
Every closure value carries a code word (heap +8) and the artifact model
gives one callable boundary PER CAPTURE LAYOUT, each stamping its own
address -- native_codegen/surface.rs:85-88 says so verbatim
("One callable can be minted through several boundaries -- one per
capture layout it is closed over at -- and each stamps its own code
address into the values it makes"). That word is the annotation that
distinguishes closure[L](int) from closure[L](float). Two sites discard
it:

  (1) THE MINT. native_codegen/prim.rs lower_make_closure ->
      settled_callable_boundary_id(env, fn_id) ->
      surface.callable_boundary_for_identity(fn_id) =
      callable_boundaries.values().find(identity_fn == fn_id): the FIRST
      boundary in a HashMap whose identity matches. mk[int] and mk[float]
      each know exactly what they capture (their own key says so) and
      both ask "any boundary for L", stamp whichever comes first, and lay
      captures out per THAT boundary's capture_reprs. fz-kdt.155's guard
      ("no single settled representation") is this lookup noticing the
      two boundaries disagree -- it is the mint not knowing which
      boundary it is, reported as a refusal.
  (2) THE READER. fz-kdt.125's identity test uses
      callable_boundaries_for_target, which admits EVERY boundary for the
      target, so even where the word carries the layout the test asks
      only "is it L?" -- true for both.

Downstream of those two erasures the picture from the dump follows
mechanically: run is one body (fz-6gb's forwarder erasure to
`(a0_p0) -> a0_r`, correct for a forwarder), its callsite mints
twice[closure[L](float)] (RawF64 return lane) and twice[closure[L](int)]
(RawInt), the plan has no test node (graph root=n1, n1 = outcome o0),
arm 0 takes everything, the int closure runs inside the float body and
its int result is marshaled through a RawF64 lane: 12.0.

THE PRINCIPLE (from the review of this ticket, 2026-09-02): a callable
value carries its own dispatch annotation. Static knowledge flows by
KEY; dynamic knowledge flows by the WORD the value already carries.
Any runtime test that re-derives a fact the mint stamped -- a capture
read, a type test, a capture-repr probe -- is rebuilding, i.e. wasted
work, and so is every specialization on a callable identity the caller
could not pin statically (N bodies plus a blind dispatch, where one
indirect call through the word is correct by construction and costs one
load). Grounding to a DIRECT call is legitimate exactly when the key
pins one target, and then there is no dispatch to get wrong.

CURE, in that order:
  (a) The mint selects its boundary by (identity, the capture layout the
      minting body actually writes) -- the minting body's own key -- not
      by identity alone. callable_boundary_for_identity has no
      legitimate caller after this; delete it. The interp mint (slot
      holds FnId) must carry the same distinction (its executable /
      boundary id, not the bare FnId).
  (b) The identity test compares the word against the boundary of the
      TARGET SPECIALIZATION, not the union of boundaries for the FnId.
      callable_boundaries_for_target's doc comment ("has to admit all
      of them") becomes false and goes with it.
  (c) With (a)+(b), a dispatch between same-fn-id targets is one word
      compare the identity axis already loads. Then measure whether the
      per-literal CONSUMER specializations below an erased forwarder are
      worth keeping at all versus one consumer calling indirectly
      through the word; the six residue groups (00231, 00277 x2, 00281,
      opaque_fn_value_join, repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 --
      reduce lambda capturing fnref[add_a] vs fnref[add_b], same
      layout, chosen by a runtime case in 00281) are the population
      where the caller CANNOT pin the identity statically, so the
      specialization on it is exactly the wasted work.

Do NOT build: a capture-read axis, a capture-type test, a type-keyed
key split as the primary cure (keeping capture types in the forwarder
key is the static half and may still be right for lane precision, but
it does not touch the mint defect and would leave (1)/(2) in place for
the dynamic case). The 'unrepresentable plan' diagnostic stays refuted
(would refuse five corpus fixtures).

RELATIONS: fz-kdt.155 (the guard that reports (1)); fz-kdt.125 (the
test that erases at (2)); fz-kdt.152 (layouts-not-targets counting,
same family); fz-kdt.137 (depth-1 tuple instance); fz-kdt.119(3)
(enlarged (B) one tuple deep); fz-6gb (forwarder erasure stays as is);
fz-9i4 memory "CallClosure = indirect by construction".

ACCEPTANCE: samelambda3 prints 12 / 11.0 on interp, JIT, AOT, both call
orders, red-first with production paths; 00281 twin changed to acc - x
still -6 on all paths; callable_boundary_for_identity deleted; residue
gate (drive_test.rs INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_RESIDUE) 6 -> 0 or each
survivor named with its reason; fz-6gb sharing census unchanged; canon
movement classified.

comments.text:
MEASURED by the fz-kdt.125 build (2026-09-01, base bd03d922e). Two premises in
this ticket's body and in fz-kdt.125's spec item 6 are REFUTED:

(1) "13/13 in-corpus groups are identity-separable" is an artifact of the
census helper. Its separability test regexes EVERY closure/fnref name out of a
key, including the ones sitting in CAPTURES -- and a capture is not identity.
Re-measured against the landed axis: the no-question population falls 13 -> 6,
not 13 -> 0. The 6 survivors are THIS ticket's shape exactly, same fn id and
different captures:

  00231_joined_fn_refs_enum_reduce      1  closure[Enum.reduce/3#lambda](fnref[add_a/2])
                                           vs (fnref[add_b/2])
  00277_enum_tier0_fixture              2  same lambda over two different inner closures
  00281_opaque_reducer_closure          1  as 00231
  behavior/opaque_fn_value_join         1  as 00231
  behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2  1  as 00277

(2) "Corpus fallout of the backstop measured ZERO" therefore does not hold. An
unrepresentable-plan DIAGNOSTIC on inseparable groups would refuse to compile
five corpus fixtures. The fz-kdt.125 build did NOT land it for that reason --
the routing half of this ticket is still open and still unbuilt, and it needs
either capture discrimination or a corpus that stops relying on the shape.

WHAT DID LAND, and it is this ticket's ABI half: `Prim::ClosureCapture` reads a
capture back out of a closure through the boundary that WROTE it, and refuses
at compile time when one callable was minted at several capture layouts that
disagree about a slot -- which is samelambda3's shape. That turns "native
executable lowering failed for index 11" into a named invariant failure. The
compile failure itself (interp: "omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs
semantic inputs") is untouched and still this ticket's.

NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER, measured: 00281 with its twin function changed from
`acc + x` to `acc - x` answers -6 on interp and JIT at head. The six groups'
arm-0-takes-all is order-decided but the members are interchangeable on the
probes tried; that is luck, not a proof.

fz-kdt.119 review sequencing (2026-09-01): 119(3)'s recursive identity-preserving erasure ENLARGES this ticket's population ({:tag,#66(int)} vs {:tag,#66(float)} collapse to one question at depth -- same-fn-id/different-capture, one tuple deep). Also this ticket's compile-failure half now has a depth-1 instance with its own ticket (fz-kdt.137) which blocks 119's REFNEST-style acceptance. The backstop-policy decision this ticket owns grows correspondingly.

title: P1: a closure's code word is the per-layout annotation the model already stamps -- the mint picks its boundary by IDENTITY and the identity test admits every boundary, so same-lambda/different-capture values are born indistinguishable (interp 12.0 for 12; native refuses)
